  "6": "A DPIA will help you consider how best to mitigate the impact on individuals' ability to exercise control over their data in invisible processing.",

  "8": "The DPIA is an on-going process, especially where a processing operation is dynamic and subject to ongoing change, and carrying out a DPIA is a continual process, not a one-time exercise.",
  "9": "The DPIA should be seen as a tool for helping decision-making concerning the processing, with the DPIA started as early as is practicable in the design of the processing operation even if some of the processing operations are still unknown.",

  "11": "Data concerning vulnerable data subjects is a criterion for determining whether processing is likely to result in high risk because of the increased power imbalance between the data subjects and the data controller, meaning the individuals may be unable to easily consent to or oppose the processing of their data or exercise their rights.",
  "12": "Beyond special categories and criminal data, other categories of personal data can be considered as increasing the possible risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals, including data linked to household and private activities such as electronic communications, data impacting the exercise of a fundamental right such as location data, and data involving serious impacts in the data subject's daily life such as financial data."
